correctness.rationale: Every direction is unit; vector equilibrium and the exact subset norm formula are derived algebraically. Concavity of x^theta controls j<=k/2; convexity of t^{-(1-theta)} controls j>=k/2 under the explicit dimension threshold. For any oriented competitor tree, summing dual lower bounds over its edges telescopes to k+k^p, exactly the star cost. The known strict-concavity reduction to a tree handles unrestricted finite admissible flows. Replayed finite checker reports 10772 checks, but the analytic proof carries the quantifiers.

value.rationale: Directly addresses a published November 2026 open direction on lower bounds for high-dimensional Gilbert–Steiner branching degree. It nearly doubles the previously cited general d+1 construction (linear-factor improvement, not a routine numerical increment), with explicit finite terminal coordinates, certified global optimality, and an exponent-dependent dimension threshold. No claim of solving the matching upper bound.
